M17_S01.summary: Consciousness conditions mind-and-matter: in the formless realms it conditions mentality, among non-percipient beings materiality, and elsewhere both together.
body: VIÑÑĀṆAPACCAYĀ NĀMARŪPAṂ — with consciousness as condition, mind-and-matter arises. Nāma is mentality, rūpa materiality, paṭicca the conditioning relation, viññāṇa consciousness.

Mentality and materiality are two distinct components, yet both arise in dependence on consciousness. Mentality comprises feeling (the mental factor of feeling), perception (the mental factor of perception) and the formations (the remaining 50 mental factors), all arising together with consciousness; these four are inseparable and are called the four mental aggregates.
The mundane resultant cittas are accompanied only by the ethically variable and the beautiful mental factors; none of the 14 unwholesome factors occurs in them.

How consciousness conditions mentality depends on the plane: in the formless realms consciousness conditions mentality alone; among the non-percipient beings it conditions materiality alone; in the form sphere and the sense sphere it conditions both mentality and materiality.

As to consciousness conditioning materiality: the rebirth-linking consciousness conditions three decads of matter. Every mind-moment divides into three sub-moments (arising, presence, dissolution); 17 mind-moments × 3 = 51 sub-moments; 51 × 3 groups = 153 groups, namely the body-sensitivity decad, the sex decad and the heart-base decad.

These three groups are kamma-born matter arising at the very MOMENT OF ARISING of the rebirth-linking consciousness, and are therefore called the kamma-born matter of rebirth — thirty material phenomena arising together. The body-sensitivity decad consists of the 8 inseparable materialities (the four great elements of earth, water, fire and air, together with visible form, odour, taste and nutritive essence) plus the life faculty, and so on for the rest.

M17_S02.summary: Mind-and-matter conditions the six bases — five sensitivities and the mind base of 32 mundane resultants — and the six bases condition the six kinds of contact.
body: NĀMARŪPAPACCAYĀ SAḶĀYATANAṂ — with mind-and-matter as condition, the six sense bases arise. The first five bases are the five sensitive materialities: the eye base (Cakkhāyatana, the eye-sensitivity by which visible form is seen), the ear base (Sotāyatana), the nose base (Ghānāyatana), the tongue base (Jivhāyatana) and the body base (Kāyāyatana).

The mind base (Manāyatana) comprises the 32 mundane resultant cittas: 15 rootless resultants + 8 great sense-sphere resultants with roots + 5 form-sphere resultants + 4 formless-sphere resultants. In the formless realms it is mentality alone that serves as condition for this mind base.

SAḶĀYATANAPACCAYĀ PHASSO — with the six bases as condition, contact arises. The six internal bases meeting the six external bases condition contact, and contact is therefore sixfold: eye-contact is the mental factor of contact arising together with the pair of eye-consciousnesses, and likewise ear-, nose-, tongue- and body-contact; mind-contact is the mental factor of contact arising in the 22 mundane resultant cittas other than the ten sense consciousnesses.

Contact also varies by plane: a formless brahmā has mind-contact only; a percipient form-sphere brahmā has eye-contact, ear-contact and mind-contact; a non-percipient being has no contact at all; a being of the sense sphere has all six, as the occasion arises.

M17_S03.summary: Contact conditions the six feelings in the 32 mundane resultants, and feeling — painful, pleasant or neutral alike — conditions craving, which in ultimate terms is the factor of greed.
body: PHASSAPACCAYĀ VEDANĀ — with contact as condition, feeling arises. The six kinds of contact (eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and mind), that is, the mental factor of contact in the 32 mundane resultant cittas, condition the arising of the six kinds of feeling.

Among the five pairs of sense consciousness, the first four pairs (eye, ear, nose, tongue) are accompanied by equanimity only; body-feeling is twofold, painful and pleasant. Mental feeling is twofold, joy and equanimity, and belongs to the 22 mundane resultant cittas (2 unwholesome resultants, 3 rootless wholesome resultants, 8 sense-sphere beautiful resultants and 9 sublime resultants).

The six feelings occur according to plane: the formless realms have one (mental feeling); the percipient form realms have three (eye-, ear- and mental feeling); the non-percipient realm has no feeling at all, since it has no contact; the sense sphere has all six, as do the realms of hell beings, ghosts and asuras.

VEDANĀPACCAYĀ TAṆHĀ — with feeling as condition, craving arises. All three feelings condition craving: painful, pleasant and neutral. Craving in ultimate terms is the mental factor of greed (Lobha); words of the same family are craving (taṇhā), sensual desire (kāma) and lust (rāga).

Painful feeling conditions craving through the longing to be free of pain; pleasant and neutral feeling condition craving through the wish to go on enjoying them. The mental factor of feeling arising in the 32 mundane resultant cittas is thus the support from which craving springs.

M17_S04.summary: Craving conditions clinging — sixfold by object and fourfold by nature — and clinging conditions becoming, which divides into kamma-becoming and rebirth-becoming.
body: TAṆHĀPACCAYĀ UPĀDĀNAṂ — with craving as condition, clinging arises. Clinging is sixfold by way of its objects: clinging to visible forms, to sounds, to odours, to tastes, to tangibles and to mental objects.

By way of ultimate realities, clinging is of four kinds: 1. sensual clinging (Kāmupādāna), grasping at sense objects with the full force of the attachment that grows out of craving — in ultimate terms the mental factor of greed; 2. clinging to views (Diṭṭhupādāna), grasping at mistaken opinions such as that the world is eternal, that there is an abiding self, or that there is no cause and no result — in ultimate terms the mental factor of wrong view; 3. clinging to rites and observances (Sīlabbatupādāna), holding that the mind is purified by misguided practices, ceremonies and sacrifices; 4. clinging to a doctrine of self (Attavādupādāna).

UPĀDĀNAPACCAYĀ BHAVO — with clinging as condition, becoming arises. Becoming is what comes to be, what exists, what will exist and will come to be. It is of two kinds: kamma-becoming (Kammabhava) and rebirth-becoming (Upapattibhava).

Kamma-becoming is threefold: bodily kamma (intentional action through the body), verbal kamma (through speech) and mental kamma (intentional mundane thought, wholesome or unwholesome). In ultimate terms it is the mental factor of volition in the 12 unwholesome cittas and the 8 sense-sphere beautiful wholesome cittas, with the 9 sublime wholesome cittas added in the case of mental kamma.

Rebirth-becoming is classified in three ways. By sphere: sense-sphere becoming (the 11 sense-sphere realms, with all five aggregates: 4 woeful realms + the human realm + 6 sense-sphere heavens), form-sphere becoming and formless becoming. By perception: percipient becoming (29 realms), non-percipient becoming (1 realm) and neither-perception-nor-non-perception becoming (1 realm). By aggregates: one-aggregate becoming (the non-percipient realm, materiality only), four-aggregate becoming (the 4 formless realms, mentality only) and five-aggregate becoming (the 11 sense-sphere realms + 15 form realms, the non-percipient realm excepted).

Sense-sphere becoming arises out of sensual desire; becoming that arises from detachment from sense desire but with attachment to form is form-becoming; becoming that arises from detachment from form with attachment to the formless is formless becoming. Three kinds of becoming × four kinds of clinging give twelve corresponding modes of becoming.
One point must be kept in mind: WITHOUT KAMMA-BECOMING THERE IS NO REBIRTH-BECOMING.

M17_S05.summary: Only kamma-becoming — the 29 kamma-producing cittas — conditions birth; and birth brings with it ageing, death, and the sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair that close the circle.
body: BHAVAPACCAYĀ JĀTI — with becoming as condition, birth arises. Here only KAMMA-BECOMING is meant; rebirth-becoming cannot play this conditioning role.

Kamma-becoming comprises the 12 unwholesome cittas + 8 great sense-sphere wholesome cittas + 5 form-sphere wholesome cittas + 4 formless-sphere wholesome cittas = 29 cittas. Every difference of class, family, dwelling place and mode of destiny at birth comes about through these kammas.

Birth (Jāti) is the arising, the coming into existence, of the aggregates — the appearance of the two components, mentality and materiality — together with the arising of kamma-born matter: the body-sensitivity decad, the sex decad and the heart-base decad.

There are four modes of birth: egg-born (Aṇḍajajāti), womb-born (Jalābujajāti), moisture-born (Saṃsedajajāti) and spontaneously born (Opapātikajāti). And three modes by aggregate: five-aggregate birth (26 realms: 11 sense-sphere + 15 form-sphere less the non-percipient realm), four-aggregate birth (the 4 formless realms) and one-aggregate birth (the non-percipient realm).

JĀTIPACCAYĀ JARĀMARAṆAṂ — with birth as condition, ageing and death arise. Ageing is the wearing out, the growing old, the decaying of what has arisen. Ageing of the material body (Rūpakāyajarā) is the 49 sub-moments of presence of material phenomena, the stage of standing between arising and dissolution; ageing of the mental body (Nāmakāyajarā) is the moment of presence of consciousness (each mind-moment having three sub-moments: arising, presence, dissolution). Death is the breaking up that follows upon having lived.

Sorrow (Soka) is the grief of loss — of relatives, wealth, position, livelihood, health or virtue. Lamentation (Parideva) is the wailing and crying out that issues from sorrow; lamentation is the voice of sorrow. Pain (Dukkha) is bodily suffering, painful bodily feeling such as illness. Grief (Domanassa) is pain in the mind, the displeased feeling of consciousness. Despair (Upāyāsa) is the crushing weight borne by one who has suffered too heavy a mental loss; it is heavier still than grief.
SORROW, LAMENTATION, PAIN, GRIEF AND DESPAIR are the inevitable consequences of birth; and ageing-and-death in turn conditions ignorance — the closed circle of the round of existence.

M17_S06.summary: Across three periods the twelve links resolve into twenty modes: five past causes, five present effects, five present causes and five future effects.
body: The three periods (Addhā): the past comprises ignorance and the formations; the present comprises consciousness, mind-and-matter, the six bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging and becoming (eight links); the future comprises birth and ageing-and-death.
The twelve links (Aṅga): ignorance → formations → consciousness → mind-and-matter → the six bases → contact → feeling → craving → clinging → becoming → birth → ageing-and-death.

The twenty modes (Visākāra): five causal modes in the past — ignorance and the formations, taken together with craving, clinging and becoming; five resultant modes in the present — consciousness, mind-and-matter, the six bases, contact and feeling; five causal modes in the present — craving, clinging and becoming, together with ignorance and the formations; five resultant modes in the future — consciousness, mind-and-matter, the six bases, contact and feeling.
Thus the twenty modes = 5 past causes + 5 present effects + 5 present causes + 5 future effects: two rounds of cause and effect following one upon the other across the three periods.
